messages:
kyle: Heads-up — hitting weird p95 east-west spikes across pool-gpu-usw2 when batch windows ramp at 09:30-10:00 PST. Started ~3 days ago after the kernel/firmware roll.

mona: Saw the same on our canary traffic. p50 fine, p95 shoots up from ~12ms -> 120-300ms for short periods. Correlated with high batch queue depth.

sasha: Any packetloss in the dumps? I checked the overlay counters and didn't see sustained drops.

kyle: Not full loss, more like retrans/reordering. tcp_retrans/sec ticks up a bit on the affected hosts. RDMA metrics show fallback events — some hosts negotiating out to TCP.

anil: That's interesting — firmware 3.7.2 on 8 hosts is using a different rdma driver path. Could be path MTU/negotiation mismatch.

nathan: Packet capture from host gpu-32 shows multiple MSS clamping and then AH reassembly delays. Snippet: ```tcp 10.0.3.14:32768 -> 10.0.3.22:1967 len 1400 PSH ACK``` followed by a bunch of small retransmits, then a big gap.

mona: I ran ethtool -k and MTU on the host vs ToR looked consistent (9000) but there were a few VFs with MTU 1500 after the kernel upgrade. Suspect VF migration left some interfaces at default.

kyle: Good call — that would explain path fragmentation for jumbo frames. If some hops accept 9000 and others see 1500, you get fragmentation and CPU-side reassembly which kills latency during burst batching.

infra-bot: monitoring-bot detected 6 host-level rdma-fallback events between 09:28 and 09:45 (severity: warning). Link: https://internal.monitoring/r/evt/1945

sasha: Any evidence it's the ToR? I checked switch counters for errors and CRCs are low. However, there are a handful of drops on the egress queue of switch-33 between ports 12-15 during the window.

anil: From infra side: we rolled firmware 3.7.2 and a kernel accel patch last week. The vendor accidentally changed default VF MTU behavior on a narrow subset of NICs. I'm 90% sure it's the root cause.

nathan: Proposed mitigations: 1) Force MTU sync across all VFs before next window, 2) Pin RDMA to specific driver path that doesn't fallback, 3) Temporarily overprovision capacity to absorb latency tails (cost hit). Thoughts?

mona: I can push an automated check to enforce VF MTU=9000 across the pool and restart the NIC service; low risk. We should do that first.

kyle: Agree — do MFV (mass fix) for VF MTU first and monitor the next batch window. If that fails, roll driver pinning as a second step. Overprovisioning is last resort.

anil: I'll open a vendor ticket about the driver default change. Also putting a scripted rollout to cascade MTU fixes to 200 hosts in canary -> stage -> prod.

sasha: Q: can we temporarily change batching config (smaller window) to reduce the simultaneous packet burst? Would that impact throughput much?

kyle: We could reduce batch-window by 20% as a short-lived experiment; might increase tokens/sec cost by ~7-10% but reduce p95 impact. Fine as temporary.

mona: Action items: 
- anil: vendor ticket + rollout plan for MTU force (ETA today EOD).
- anil/mona: MFV script to set VF MTU=9000 and restart nicd (canary now).
- kyle: schedule a 24h canary during next low-traffic window and watch p95.
- sasha: prepare quick playbook to fallback batch-window if spikes reappear.

nathan: I'll also craft a quick cost estimate for 24h overprovision (reserve + burst) if we need to buy headroom.

kyle: Thanks — please ping here when canary completes. Adding :eyes: to monitoring dashboards for the window.

monitoring-bot: Alert muted for this thread window. Next run of the RDMA-fallback detector at 09:30 PST.

mona: Canary pushed at 13:05 UTC to 8 hosts (gpu-canary-1..8). Initial MTU fix applied. Will report in after next peak.

anil: Vendor ticket created: VID-9921, referencing driver/default-VF-MTU change.

kyle: Great. If anyone sees a different pattern (e.g., sudden packet loss instead of fragmentation), call it out immediately.

sasha: One more note — app-level tracing shows batch assemble time spikes at the same time, reinforcing network origin.

kyle: Cool. Closing loop: we'll reconvene after the canary window and decide about driver pin or batch-window tweak. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
